headline: Imposter: A Secret-Role Speaking Game for ESL
problemStatement: A secret-role game can give every student a reason to listen for clues and choose their words carefully. In Imposter, most students receive the same secret while one player gets a different card. The class speaks in turn, watches for mismatched clues, and votes on who may not belong.
outcomes: Practice concise spoken clues or answers while withholding a secret word or question.
Listen for details that fit the shared prompt and notice when a response feels different.
Use inference and class discussion to make a case before voting.
howItWorks: Choose Secret word, Secret question, or Today's words. The activity deals private role cards to phones; students hold the phone to peek and release to hide it.
In a word round, the crew knows the word and gives one clue each. In a question round, everyone answers aloud to their own question, while the imposter receives a related but different one.
The clue order changes each round, never repeats the same first speaker, and keeps an imposter from speaking first. Easy hint can give an imposter a category clue for word or topic rounds.
After clues, the class votes and sees the result. With enough students, the teacher can choose two imposters; a last-chance guess and the reveal complete the round.
teacherUseCases: Use Secret question when you want fuller spoken answers; choose a word or today's vocabulary when the lesson is focused on concise clues.
Ask students to cite the clue that influenced their vote, so the reveal becomes a listening and reasoning discussion.
groupSize: 3 or more students; two imposters requires 6 or more

faq.q: Can classmates see the private role cards?
faq.a: No. Roles and secrets are sent to individual phones. A student holds the screen to peek and releases it to hide the card from nearby classmates.

faq.q: What are the three secret types?
faq.a: Students can play with a shared word, a shared question with a different question for the imposter, or a word drawn from today's topic vocabulary.

faq.q: How does the activity keep speaking turns fair?
faq.a: The clue order changes every round and does not reuse the previous first speaker. The imposter is not placed first, and the roster rotates across rounds.
Easy hint can give the imposter a category clue in word and vocabulary rounds. The teacher can also select Secret question, where everyone answers a prompt aloud.
